subject: Future Tech
title: The Scanning Tunneling Microscope
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Scanning Tunneling Microscope.

hook.text: In 1981, two IBM scientists built a microscope that could see individual atoms for the first time.

buildup.text: The scanning tunneling microscope (STM) uses a needle tip one atom wide.

discovery.text: The STM doesn't see atoms—it can move them.

twist.text: Seeing atoms changed everything. Scientists could finally design at the atomic level instead of guessing.

climax.text: The STM spawned a family of tools: atomic force microscopes, electron microscopes, and nanoprobes enabling nanotech.

punchline.text: You can't engineer what you can't see. The STM opened the door.
